subsystems.name: Compute dies
subsystems.role: the logic chiplets — CPU cores, GPU blocks or accelerators — built on the most advanced node available.

subsystems.name: Support dies
subsystems.role: everything that gains nothing from the leading edge but is expensive there.
parts: SRAM/cache dies on a mature node

subsystems.name: Memory stacks
subsystems.role: high-bandwidth DRAM placed physically beside the logic.

subsystems.name: Die-to-die interconnect
subsystems.role: moves data between chiplets cheaply enough to behave like one chip.

subsystems.name: Packaging substrate
subsystems.role: mechanically holds the dies and fans their connections out to the board.
parts: silicon interposer or embedded bridge with TSVs

subsystems.name: Thermal solution
subsystems.role: removes heat from a hot, uneven, multi-die surface.

buildSteps.title: Partition the design
buildSteps.detail: Engineers split the chip into functions that belong on different nodes: transistors on the newest process, SRAM on a cheaper one, analog and IO on mature nodes. This is where most of the value is captured or lost.

buildSteps.title: Define the die-to-die link
buildSteps.detail: Each boundary becomes a standard interface — UCIe is the industry effort here — with agreed bump pitch, bandwidth density and power per bit, so dies from different teams or vendors can talk.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the dies
buildSteps.detail: Each chiplet runs through its own wafer process, so a cache die may be several generations behind the compute die next to it.

buildSteps.title: Test before assembly
buildSteps.detail: Every die is probed and burned in at operating speed while still on the wafer, so that only known-good dies enter the package — a bad die discovered later wastes the whole assembly.

buildSteps.title: Build the interposer
buildSteps.detail: A silicon interposer is processed with fine wiring and through-silicon vias, or a small bridge die is embedded directly into the organic substrate for a cheaper, coarser connection.

buildSteps.title: Bond the dies
buildSteps.detail: Flip-chip thermocompression bonding places each die onto microbumps whose pitch is measured in tens of microns, one die at a time, with placement accuracy of a few microns. Denser 3D stacks instead use hybrid bonding, joining copper pads directly with no solder.

buildSteps.title: Underfill and package
buildSteps.detail: Epoxy underfill is wicked into the gaps to spread mechanical stress, then the substrate, stiffener, lid and heat spreader are attached.

buildSteps.title: Test the whole package
buildSteps.detail: The assembled part is tested as a system — including the die-to-die links running at speed — then thermally cycled and stressed to prove the joints survive years of expansion and contraction.

prerequisites.why: interposer-based packaging such as TSMC's CoWoS is in volume production, but capacity has been a genuine constraint on how many parts can ship.
stacked DRAM beside logic on an interposer is what made the packaging approach commercially compelling in the first place.
UCIe published its first specification in 2022, but real interoperability between chiplets from different vendors is still early.
testing bare dies at operating speed before assembly is the key economic enabler and remains difficult and expensive.
direct copper-to-copper bonding at pitches under 10 µm is shipping in some products such as image sensors, but logic-on-logic volume is still ramping.

prerequisites.tech: Multi-die design and thermal co-design tools
prerequisites.why: floorplanning, power delivery and thermal analysis across a package rather than a die are only partly supported by current EDA flows.

pathway.milestone: multi-die server CPUs and accelerators in volume — AMD moved its EPYC server line to a multi-die layout in 2017 — plus GPUs surrounded by HBM
pathway.unlocks: cheap cores and memory bandwidth that a single monolithic die could not deliver.

pathway.milestone: interoperable UCIe chiplets sourced from third parties
pathway.unlocks: a real market in reusable dies, so smaller companies can build competitive parts without a full leading-edge design.

pathway.milestone: volume logic-on-logic hybrid bonding and backside power delivery
pathway.unlocks: 3D stacks with far denser connections than side-by-side chiplets, and shorter, lower-loss wiring.

pathway.milestone: co-packaged optics and optical die-to-die links
pathway.unlocks: breaking the reach and energy limits of copper at the package edge, enabling much larger systems in one package.
